Front:
A team wants to store embedding vectors with transactional order data and query both in one ACID database engine. Which platform choice best fits?

A) Azure SQL Database with native vector support
B) Azure Blob Storage containers with lifecycle rules
C) Azure Files shares with SMB access
Back:
A) Azure SQL Database with native vector support

Azure SQL Database can keep relational rows and vectors together, so transactional writes and vector lookups stay in one engine.

Reference: Vector search in Azure SQL Database
Extra: Blob and file storage are great for objects, but they do not provide relational joins, ACID OLTP patterns, or native SQL vector querying.

Front:
You must find the most semantically similar support article to a user question embedding. Which T-SQL function should you use in the ranking query?

A) JSON_VALUE to parse the vector payload
B) VECTOR_DISTANCE to score embedding similarity
C) STRING_SPLIT to tokenize question text
Back:
B) VECTOR_DISTANCE to score embedding similarity

VECTOR_DISTANCE computes distance between vectors so you can ORDER BY similarity for nearest-neighbor retrieval.

Reference: VECTOR_DISTANCE (Transact-SQL)
Extra: JSON_VALUE and STRING_SPLIT are useful utilities, but they do not compute numeric distance between embeddings.

A) Pure prompting with no retrieval layer
B) Keyword-only lookup with no semantic ranking

C) RAG that retrieves approved chunks before generation

RAG augments model prompts with trusted retrieved context, improving factual grounding and traceability.

Reference: Retrieval-augmented generation overview
Extra: Pure prompting cannot cite enterprise facts reliably. Keyword-only lookup often misses semantically relevant passages.
